Proposition
[Hessian of the Euclidean distance function]

Source: petersen:page-0135 On $\mathbb {R}^n$, write the polar-coordinate metric $g=dr^2+g_r$, $g_r=r^2ds_{n-1}^2$, where $ds_{n-1}^2$ is the canonical metric on $S^{n-1}(1)$ and $r(x)=|x|$. Then $\mathrm{Hess}\, r=\tfrac 1r g_r$.
Proof

↗ prop:pet-ch4-hess-r-euclidean \sketch Both $dr$ and $ds_{n-1}^2$ are invariant under the radial flow. Therefore

\[ 2\operatorname {Hess}r=L_{\partial _r}g =L_{\partial _r}(r^2ds_{n-1}^2) =2r\, ds_{n-1}^2=\frac2r g_r. \]

□
